python_runtime: Independent pure-Python exact integer synaptic sums and threshold >=0; no NumPy, training helper, symbolic runtime decoder, teacher, graph search, or latent body variables enter learned network inference.
model_world_binding: Evaluator body=(x,y), flip=(1-x,y), swap=(y,x), noop/STOP=(x,y). Initial observation is one-hot x plus one-hot y plus binary nuisance. Six-bit fingerprint concatenates current observation, observation after flip, observation after swap. This is a declared tiny deterministic body, not physical-world validation.

direct_corrupted_policy_decisions.proof_if_passed: Initialization establishes the corresponding canonical body/memory code. Each decision cycle tolerates a fresh arbitrary allowed XOR fault, then selects one unique action. STOP holds exactly at the true body goal; otherwise its action strictly decreases the nonnegative body-goal rank and restores the exact canonical code corresponding to the body's new state. Induction closes arbitrarily many cycles, with at most three non-STOP actions per fixed goal.
direct_corrupted_policy_decisions.fault_schedule: Before EVERY policy decision, an adversary XORs up to k distinct queued memory spike bits. SAME learned policy acts directly on that damaged state, and its selected non-STOP action then drives body and memory; no fresh fault occurs during the action tick. Nuisance may vary at every tick. Goal one-hot, synaptic weights, transient neurons and body are uncorrupted.
direct_corrupted_policy_decisions.terminal_stop_semantics: STOP performs no body action or memory action tick. Direct mode does not demand canonical repair after STOP; refreshed mode demands canonical repair before policy, including the terminal STOP cycle.

neural_refresh_then_same_learned_policy.proof_if_passed: Initialization establishes the corresponding canonical body/memory code. Each decision cycle tolerates a fresh arbitrary allowed XOR fault, then selects one unique action. STOP holds exactly at the true body goal; otherwise its action strictly decreases the nonnegative body-goal rank and restores the exact canonical code corresponding to the body's new state. Induction closes arbitrarily many cycles, with at most three non-STOP actions per fixed goal.
neural_refresh_then_same_learned_policy.fault_schedule: Before EVERY cycle, an adversary XORs up to k distinct queued memory spike bits. A neural NOOP memory tick with arbitrary nuisance refreshes the state; SAME exported learned goal policy then runs, and its unique non-STOP action drives body and memory with arbitrary nuisance. No fault occurs between refresh, policy inference, and the action tick. A fresh fault may occur before the next cycle. Goal one-hot, synaptic weights, transient neurons and body are uncorrupted.
neural_refresh_then_same_learned_policy.terminal_stop_semantics: STOP performs no body action or memory action tick. Direct mode does not demand canonical repair after STOP; refreshed mode demands canonical repair before policy, including the terminal STOP cycle.

scope_limits: Exact serialized 12-memory-neuron, 64-transition-neuron clocked threshold model and 64-hidden-neuron goal policy only.
All 16 canonical body/goal combinations are exhaustively checked; these are not held-out learned-policy generalization cases.
The offline goal-policy training teacher used model graph planning. No new autonomous planning capability is claimed.

The fault model affects only queued memory spikes at declared decision-cycle boundaries; continuous faults, faulty goals/synapses/transient neurons, simultaneous body changes and unmodeled sensors are not certified.
Refreshing before action is an explicit scheduling condition, not robustness of policy decisions taken directly on corrupted memory.
The world has four body states and three ordinary commands; finite induction is specific to that complete alphabet and binding.
This does not establish Brian2 LIF equivalence, production Nuria robustness, consciousness, global novelty or a practical advantage over symbolic/error-correcting alternatives.
